div.div: تَيْمٌ i. q. عَبْدٌ [as meaning A slave, and a servant or worshipper or God or of a false god]: whence the names تَيْمُ ٱللّٰهِ [The servant of God] and تَيْمُ اللَّاتِ [The servant of El-Lát]: (S, M, K:) pl. تُيُومٌ: it is originally an inf. n., from تَامُهُ: or an epithet like its syn. عَبْدٌ: J says that it is from تَيَّمَهُ الحُبُّ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
